title: Robustness, Evaluation and Adaptation of Machine Learning Models in the Wild
measurement_description: The paper measures performance disparity in toxicity classification for comments mentioning Muslims (as a demographic group within the CivilComments-WILDS dataset) and text classification performance on the 'Religion' topic within the 20 Newsgroups dataset. This is part of a broader analysis of model robustness to subpopulation and domain shifts.
findings: The paper's primary findings are on the effectiveness of its proposed methods (CSD, CGD, KYC, etc.) for improving model robustness under domain and subpopulation shifts. In the context of religion, the experiments on the CivilComments-WILDS dataset implicitly show that standard ERM models perform poorly on subgroups defined by identity, such as comments mentioning Muslims. The proposed CGD algorithm demonstrates improved performance on this subgroup, mitigating the performance drop seen with baseline models.
